clue.text: Mean mum, all midriff muscle?

parts.note: to keep mum is to stay quiet, and SH is the call for silence
a playful made-up adjective: someone who is all abs would be ab-by, as someone all brawn is brawny

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted mother with a body that is nothing but rippling stomach muscles.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags an invented word: abs are the stomach muscles, so a midriff made of them is 'abby', as all brawn is brawny.
explanation.definitionFit: Shabby behaviour is mean in the sense of petty, ungenerous and unworthy.

clue.text: Primarily seal meat dish, almost like kebab

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the following word is dropped
primarily means in the first place, so only the opening letter of the next word counts

parts.note: the first letter of seal
hash is a dish of chopped cooked meat
taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A recipe note: seal meat is mostly what goes into this kebab-like dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A shashlik is a skewered meat dish from the Caucasus and Central Asia, a kind of kebab.

clue.text: Foul can be a half-year suspension

indicators.note: half means only one of the two halves of the word is kept, the other dropped
something fouled is messed up, so the letters that follow are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
the first half of year

explanation.surface: A sports ruling: a foul can earn a player a ban of six months.
explanation.walkthrough: Foul reads as the offence in a match, but it is the signal to mix up the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held in abeyance is temporarily suspended, set aside and not in force.

clue.text: Undergarment's wrong on guys in parade — a bugler must play through it!

definitions.text: a bugler must play through it!

indicators.note: in places the word for guys inside the word for a showy walk

parts.note: a bra is an undergarment; with the 's it gives the possessive bra's
a sin is a wrong
to strut is to parade proudly
guys are men

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a bra on men marching in a parade, while a bugler plays along.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a bugler plays by blowing air through the tubing of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugle is a member of the brass family, played by blowing air through its tubing.

clue.text: Reprimand impostor putting on front

indicators.note: putting on, as one puts on clothes, means the second word is worn around the first

parts.note: the fore is the front
a sham is a fake or impostor

explanation.surface: Telling off a fraudster who is putting on a false front.
explanation.definitionFit: "For shame!" is an exclamation of rebuke, used to scold someone for disgraceful conduct.

clue.text: Religious works skewered by slam poet

indicators.note: skewered by means pierced through, so the second word runs through the middle of the first

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a body of religious works
to dis someone is to slam or criticise them

explanation.surface: Sacred writings are torn apart by a performer at a poetry slam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slam poet' looks like one phrase from performance poetry, but slam is the wordplay and poet alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An odist is a writer of odes, so a kind of poet.

clue.text: Docs worry a nerd's out of hand with wizard content

indicators.note: out of hand means out of control, so the preceding letters run wild into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Doctors fret that a geek's fantasy obsession, full of wizards, has gone too far.
explanation.definitionFit: Sword-and-sorcery is the fantasy genre of warriors and magic, so a story of that type has wizards in it.

clue.text: Right in seeing that sci-fi classic

indicators.note: in puts the word for a right inside the phrase for seeing that

parts.note: as means because or seeing that
a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: Someone vindicated in their view of a famous science-fiction film.
explanation.walkthrough: Right is a legal right here, not correct or a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliens is James Cameron's 1986 science-fiction film, the celebrated sequel to Alien.

clue.text: ELP without Palmer still in prime?

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter standing for the named member is taken away

parts.note: the initials of the rock trio Emerson, Lake and Palmer
Palmer is the P of the band's initials
even can mean still, as in even better

explanation.surface: Is the prog-rock band, minus its drummer, still at its peak?
explanation.walkthrough: ELP were a 1970s prog-rock trio; Carl Palmer was the drummer. 'In prime' suggests being at one's peak, but prime is the number sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleven is a prime number, divisible only by one and itself; the question mark flags it as an example.

clue.text: Site for watching matches live not available

parts.note: are means exist or live, as in 'we are'
NA is the standard abbreviation for not available

explanation.surface: A stadium where you can't watch the games live because tickets are unavailable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watching matches live' reads as one phrase about live sport, but live is a verb in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a venue where spectators watch contests and sporting fixtures.

clue.text: I hurl tucking into stale old arthropod

indicators.note: tucking into means going inside, so the first part sits within the word for stale

parts.note: trite means stale or hackneyed
taken as written
to lob is to throw or hurl

explanation.surface: Someone throws up after eating something stale and ancient.
explanation.walkthrough: Hurl suggests vomiting after eating stale food, but it means to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Trilobites were marine arthropods that died out hundreds of millions of years ago, known as fossils.

clue.text: Exchange New Orleans jazz style with German one

parts.note: trad is traditional jazz in the New Orleans style
ein is German for one

explanation.surface: A swap of jazz styles with a German musician.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade-in is an exchange in which an old item is handed over as part payment for a new one.

clue.text: Chef barely notices dessert going early?

indicators.note: barely means stripped bare, so the word before it loses its outer letters

parts.note: chef stripped of its first and last letters
ads are advertisements or notices
a tart is a pastry dessert

explanation.surface: A cook hardly registers the pudding, which goes out before its time.
explanation.walkthrough: Chef wants to be HEAD, as in head chef, but barely tells you to strip it to its middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A head start is an advantage gained by setting off before the others, a cryptic gloss on going early.

clue.text: Moderate tempo put out an Italian composer

indicators.note: put out means ejected, so the two-letter word that follows is thrown out of the tempo

parts.note: andante is a musical direction for a moderate, walking pace
taken as written; this is what is removed

explanation.surface: A slowish tempo upset a composer from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: With tempo in the clue, composer suggests music; here it means the composer of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante Alighieri composed the Divine Comedy, so he is an Italian composer of poetry rather than music.

clue.text: Flaming hot tinned dip?

parts.note: something tinned is in a can
a dip is a descent or downward slope

explanation.surface: A spicy dip that comes in a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: Dip suggests a sauce for dunking, but it is a downward slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Incandescent describes something glowing white with heat, so blazing hot.

clue.text: Appear to shake tail and nap as setters do

indicators.note: to shake a tail is to get rid of what follows behind, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to come is to appear or arrive
pile is the raised surface or nap of a fabric

explanation.surface: Someone told to show up, wiggle their rear and have a doze.
explanation.walkthrough: Nap is the fuzzy surface of cloth here, not a snooze.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword setters compile puzzles, assembling the grid and clues into a finished whole.

clue.text: One revealing article about holidaymaker killing love

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the article runs the other way

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: killing means doing away with, so the letter for love is removed

parts.note: a tourist is a holidaymaker
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A newspaper exposé about a tourist who murdered a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: One revealing reads as an exposé, but it describes someone baring all.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist goes about unclothed, so is literally one revealing their body.

clue.text: Ascot perhaps rigged race with new king participating

indicators.note: something rigged is fixed and tampered with, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A fixed race at Royal Ascot, with a new king taking part.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is the famous racecourse, which suits rigged race; here it is the wide cravat named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascot is a broad formal tie worn at the throat, an example of neckwear.

clue.text: Learned about body firmness at group spa treatment

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for learned wraps around what follows

parts.note: sage means wise or learned
muscle tone is the firmness of the body
a mass is a group or body of things

explanation.surface: Someone found out about toning the body during a group session at the spa.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone massage uses heated smooth stones on the body, a common spa therapy.

clue.text: Alaskans trashing Alabama, blasted state

indicators.note: blasted means blown apart, so what is left is scattered into a new order
trashing means throwing away, so the abbreviation for the southern state is discarded

parts.note: taken as written
AL is the postal abbreviation for Alabama

explanation.surface: People from Alaska crushing Alabama in a game, with a damned state involved.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing AL leaves ASKANS to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Kansas is a state of the USA, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Fellows peel off after sign a shark's come close

parts.note: a fin breaking the surface is the classic sign that a shark has arrived

indicators.note: to peel off is to strip away the skin, so only the inside of the word stays

parts.note: fellows are males; peeled, the outer letters go

explanation.surface: Men strip off once they see a shark approaching, getting dangerously near.
explanation.walkthrough: Close looks like an adjective meaning near, but it is a noun meaning ending. After puts the fellows behind the shark's sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A finale is the close or concluding part of a show or piece of music.

clue.text: Gold-plated tumbler must be off in Versailles

indicators.note: plated means coated on the outside, so the metal surrounds the other word

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a die tumbles when thrown

explanation.surface: A gilded drinking glass has to go from the palace of Versailles.
explanation.walkthrough: A tumbler suggests a drinking glass, but here it is the dice that tumbles when rolled.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is French for goodbye, what a speaker in Versailles says when they must be off.

clue.text: Monk recounted day, maybe painting fowl, shaving head

indicators.note: shaving the head removes the top, so the first letter of the bird goes

parts.note: Fri is short for Friday, an example of a day
painting is an art
a duck is a fowl

explanation.surface: A monk describes his day: maybe painting a bird, then shaving his tonsure.
explanation.walkthrough: Recounted belongs to the definition: this monk exists in tales told of Robin Hood.
explanation.definitionFit: Friar Tuck is the jovial friar of the Robin Hood legends, a holy man known through retold stories.

clue.text: Cardinal supports loud church celebration

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
east is one of the four cardinal points of the compass

explanation.surface: A cardinal of the Church backs a noisy congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, a part that supports another sits beneath it. Cardinal looks like the churchman but is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A feast is a religious festival in the church calendar, such as a saint's feast day.

clue.text: New agent, same Snoop Dogg?

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the following letters are reshaped into something different

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rapper has a new agent but stays the same old Snoop Dogg.
explanation.definitionFit: Snoop Dogg is the stage name of rapper Calvin Broadus, so it is an example of a performer's assumed name.

clue.text: Cream brilliant in cheese's centre

indicators.note: in puts the word for brilliant inside the middle pair
centre means only the middle letters of the possessive word are used

parts.note: the middle two letters of cheese
lit means lit up, brilliant with light

explanation.surface: The dairy cream is excellent inside a cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of a group is its best members, the elite.

clue.text: Watch ham going unfinished at gallery's opening

indicators.note: unfinished means not completed, so the word for ham loses its last letter

parts.note: speck is a cured smoked ham from the Tyrol
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: Someone sees a hammy actor leave midway through a gallery launch.
explanation.walkthrough: Ham suggests a bad actor, but it is the cured meat. Going at the gallery's opening puts the trimmed ham in front of TATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To spectate is to watch an event as an onlooker.

clue.text: Clump of toys terrify one in bed

indicators.note: a clump of something is a part of it, so the letters are a portion of the words that follow

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A child scared by a heap of toys while lying in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: One in bed suggests a sleeper, but oysters grow in oyster beds on the seabed.
explanation.definitionFit: Oysters are farmed and grow in colonies called oyster beds, so an oyster is one in a bed.
